lines.text: Scatterplots are on every SAT. Let's learn to read one in a minute.
Each dot is one observation: a pair of values, x and y.
Here, each dot is a student: hours studied, and math score.
Check four things. One: direction. As x grows, y goes up, so the trend is positive.
Two: form. Do the dots follow a line, or a curve?
Three: strength. Tightly packed dots mean a strong relationship. Spread out, a weak one.
Four: unusual points. This student studied a lot but scored low. An outlier.
The line of best fit runs through the middle of the cloud, about half the dots above, half below.
Its equation: y hat equals a plus b x. The slope b is the change in y per unit of x. And a is the prediction at x equals zero.
Here b is twelve: each extra hour adds about twelve points.
Practice it on real SAT problems in SAT Math Learner.
